content: USF1, also known as Upstream Stimulatory Factor 1, is a protein in humans that is encoded by the USF1 gene. This gene encodes a member of the basic helix-loop-helix leucine zipper family of proteins, which can function as a cellular transcription factor. The protein encoded by USF1 is capable of activating transcription through pyrimidine-rich initiator (Inr) elements and E-box motifs. The USF1 gene has been associated with familial combined hyperlipidemia (FCHL), a genetic disorder characterized by elevated levels of cholesterol and triglycerides. Two transcript variants of the USF1 gene have been identified, each encoding distinct isoforms of the protein. Research conducted on mice has indicated that reduced levels of USF1 may lead to increased metabolism in brown adipose tissue, suggesting a potential role in energy regulation. USF1 has been shown to interact with several other proteins, including USF2, FOSL1, and GTF2I, indicating its involvement in complex regulatory networks within the cell.
